title: Kafka Consumer
description: The consumer app's Kafka clients: lag, poll loop, processing, rebalances, commits, fetching, JVM.

options.content: **Kafka Consumer** — the consumer app's own Kafka client metrics; one client per @KafkaListener, named `consumer-<group>-<n>`. Filter by **source** and **client_id** above. Best-practice signals, in order: *lag* (is it keeping up?), *poll loop health* (time between polls vs max.poll.interval.ms), *processing time and failures*, *rebalances*, *commits*, then fetch efficiency.

panels.title: Records consumed / s
panels.description: Records received from poll() per second (1-minute average).

panels.title: Max lag
panels.description: Most records any consumer is behind on any of its partitions, as the client sees it.

panels.title: Assigned partitions
panels.description: Partitions owned by the selected consumers. 0 = not in a group (yet), or more consumers than partitions.

panels.title: Longest time between polls
panels.description: If it exceeds max.poll.interval.ms (5 min), the consumer is kicked out of the group.

panels.title: Rebalances (last hour)
panels.description: Group rebalances in the last hour. A few at startup are normal; regular ones are not.

panels.title: Listener failures / s
panels.description: @KafkaListener calls that threw an error type. Should be 0.

panels.title: Max lag per consumer
panels.description: Records behind the end of the partition, from the client. A steadily growing line = the consumer can't keep up; add consumers (up to the partition count) or speed up processing.

panels.title: Lag per partition
panels.description: Current lag of each assigned partition. Appears once partitions are assigned. One partition lagging alone = a hot key or a slow record on it.

targets.expr: max by (client_id, topic, partition) (kafka_consumer_fetch_manager_records_lag{application="consumer", source=~"$source", client_id=~"$client_id"})

panels.title: Group lag (from the brokers)
panels.description: The same lag measured by kafka-exporter from the committed offsets. Unlike the client metric, it is still visible when the consumer is stopped.

panels.title: Lead (distance from the start of the log)
panels.description: How far the consumer is from the oldest record still kept. Close to 0 = retention is about to delete records it hasn't read yet.

panels.title: Records consumed / s by topic
panels.description: Per-topic consumption rate (per-topic metrics appear after the first fetch from a topic).

panels.title: Time between polls
panels.description: Time spent processing one poll's records before the next poll(). The dashed line is max.poll.interval.ms (300 000 ms): past it the consumer leaves the group and its partitions are rebalanced. Lower max.poll.records or speed up the listener if it gets close.

panels.title: Poll idle ratio
panels.description: Share of time the consumer waits inside poll() for data. Near 1 = idle, has spare capacity. Near 0 = busy processing all the time: it is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Seconds since last poll
panels.description: Should stay around 0–1 s with Spring's poll loop. A rising line = the listener is stuck on a record.

panels.title: Listener calls / s
panels.description: Records handled by each listener, split by success and failure.

panels.title: Processing time per record
panels.description: Time the listener method takes. Processing time × max.poll.records (500) must stay well below max.poll.interval.ms.

targets.expr: sum by (spring_kafka_listener_id) (rate(spring_kafka_listener_seconds_sum{application="consumer", source=~"$source"}[1m])) / sum by (spring_kafka_listener_id) (rate(spring_kafka_listener_seconds_count{application="consumer", source=~"$source"}[1m]))

panels.title: Failures by error type
panels.description: Exceptions thrown by the listener. Spring retries a failed record (9 more times by default), then logs and skips it unless a dead-letter topic is configured.

panels.title: Assigned partitions
panels.description: Partitions each consumer owns. Start a second copy of the app and watch them split.

panels.title: Rebalances
panels.description: Rebalances pause consumption for the whole group. Frequent ones point to consumers crashing, exceeding max.poll.interval.ms, or missing heartbeats.

panels.title: Rebalance latency
panels.description: How long a rebalance takes for this consumer: the group's 'stop the world' time.

panels.title: Heartbeats
panels.description: Heartbeats keep the consumer in the group (every heartbeat.interval.ms, 3 s). Seconds since the last one approaching session.timeout.ms (45 s) = about to be removed.

panels.title: Commits / s
panels.description: Offset commits. Spring commits after each poll's records are processed (AckMode BATCH).

panels.title: Commit latency
panels.description: Time to commit offsets to __consumer_offsets. Slow commits slow down the poll loop.

panels.title: Fetch latency
panels.description: About 500 ms when idle: the broker holds a fetch up to fetch.max.wait.ms waiting for data. Lower under load.

panels.title: Fetch size
panels.description: Bytes per fetch response. Raise fetch.min.bytes to get fewer, bigger fetches.

panels.title: Records per fetch
panels.description: Records returned per fetch request.

panels.title: Bytes consumed / s
panels.description: Record bytes received.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Open connections: partition leaders it fetches from plus the group coordinator.

panels.title: Fetch throttling
panels.description: Time the broker delayed fetches because of a quota. 0 without quotas.

panels.title: Heap used vs max
panels.description: Heap in use and the limit. Used close to max for a long time = memory pressure, long GCs.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Time the JVM was stopped for garbage collection. Long pauses delay sends, polls and heartbeats.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the app, and by the whole machine (container), as a share of all cores.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Live and blocked threads. Each Kafka client adds a few network / heartbeat threads.
